marco: Heads-up — saw p95 spike for chat.default after the kernel-selector change yesterday. Numbers: p50=38ms, p95=182ms, p99=420ms. Noticed higher variance on short requests.

jessica: Ugh, saw that too. Profiler dump attached (trimmed):

jessica: ```
[2026-03-15T03:12:02Z] route=chat.default seq_len=16 kernel=opt_v1 forward_ms=12.3 kv_lookup_ms=4.1 kv_hit=false microbatch_wait_ms=28.7
[2026-03-15T03:12:02Z] route=chat.default seq_len=128 kernel=opt_v2 forward_ms=95.6 kv_lookup_ms=1.4 kv_hit=true microbatch_wait_ms=8.2
[2026-03-15T03:12:03Z] route=chat.lowprio seq_len=16 kernel=opt_v1 forward_ms=14.0 kv_hit=false microbatch_wait_ms=40.3
```

jessica: TL;DR: short seqs are paying a lot in microbatch wait time and KV cold misses. Kernel-selector picked opt_v1 for short sequences but its per-token overhead with cold KV and scheduling jitter is killing p95.

yvonne: Does the batch formation policy still use strict token budget per-microbatch? Could we reduce max-wait for short token requests or give them a higher scheduling priority?

samir: Proposing a P95-SLO driven token budget controller: dynamically compute target token_budget per route+tier so that expected microbatch formation time + model forward stays under p95 SLO. Use EWMA of observed service time quantiles per route to update every minute.

samir: Example controller heuristics (sketch):

samir: 1) Maintain sliding p50/p95 estimates of (microbatch_wait_ms + forward_ms) per token-length bucket.
2) For each route+tier, find smallest token_budget such that predicted p95 <= route.p95_target_ms.
3) Cap adjustments to +/- 20% per minute, and keep a global min of 16 tokens for throughput efficiency.

samir: Pseudo-config we tested in staging:

samir: ```yaml
token_budget_controller:
  update_interval_s: 60
  smoothing: 0.9
  max_delta_per_interval: 0.2
  min_budget: 16
  routes:
    - name: chat.default
      tier: standard
      p95_target_ms: 150
      base_budget: 64
      max_budget: 512
    - name: chat.lowprio
      tier: free
      p95_target_ms: 300
      base_budget: 32
      max_budget: 256
```

jessica: We tried a quick A/B in staging: group A uses fixed 64 tokens, group B uses controller. Results over 2h: group A p95=178ms, group B p95=138ms, overall throughput stable, CPU/GPU utilization slightly higher in B (2-3%). KV hit-rate improved in B due to shorter microbatch waits for short seqs (fewer cold-keystrokes).

yvonne: Nice. Any regressions? Where did kernel selection interact?

jessica: Kernel-selector needs a small change: when token_budget drops below 32, prefer low-latency kernel (opt_small) even if per-token perf slightly worse — it reduces tail. Also add a fast-path to bypass KV lookup if request explicitly marked no-cache.

marco: Sounds reasonable. Concern: oscillations during traffic spikes. How do we avoid thrashing budgets?

samir: Smoothing + max_delta helps. Also keep a burst pool we can drain into: if route exhausts budget and latency climbing, allow short-term borrow from global pooled capacity with stricter QoS.
